title: Choose response compression and accepted request encodings
goal: Offer Zstandard with a gzip fallback and limit accepted compressed uploads when clients support different content encodings.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: ASP.NET Core 11 supplies the new surface; exact observed runtime is RC2, not GA evidence.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the net11.0 application with an SDK supporting that target; sample pin is 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Declared canonical sample mode; older comparison uses C# 14 with SDK 10.0.402.

packageAssets: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App net11.0 shared framework and Microsoft.NETCore.App runtime assets. The comparison uses corresponding net10.0 assets. No separate package for the new API.
providers: Kestrel loopback HTTP server; process-local state only. No account, database or remote service.
platforms: ASP.NET Core supported server platforms; actually executed on Windows x64 only. No browser/WASI, native, AOT or cross-platform execution claim.
renderingModes: Server HTTP endpoints; no Blazor rendering mode.
prerequisites: Save each complete sample in its own directory with the shown SDK/project/build/package files. Restore framework packs before executing. The installed guidance is offline.
constraints: Explicit response providers replace automatic defaults: zstd and gzip only here. Explicitly remove br/deflate from the built-in request decoder registry; unsupported or stacked encodings normally pass through the middleware, so this app returns 415 when Content-Encoding remains. Response negotiation and request decoding are independent. HTTPS compression stays disabled because reflected secrets can leak through compressed size. Limit decompressed bodies as well as wire bytes. Built-in Zstandard needs .NET 11; no external .NET 10 codec route is verified. Browser/WASI are unsupported by the built-in codec.
stabilityLimitations: Stable API intent prepared from pinned .NET 11 RC2 artifacts under ADR 0004; GA reconciliation remains pending. No experimental opt-in applies.

sources.title: Response compression and explicit provider selection

evidence.scope: Actual Windows x64 .NET 10.0.13 compilation/execution: explicit gzip response and upload round trips; zstd-only response uses identity; quality/exclusion and unsupported response fallback; unsupported/stacked request 415; decompressed gzip exceeding 1024 bytes returns 413. No zstd codec or external interoperability claim.

Actual Windows x64 .NET 11 RC2 compilation/execution: raw zstd/gzip response negotiation and decompressed body equality, quality weighting/q=0, identity and unsupported fallback; real zstd/gzip uploads, unsupported/stacked 415 and decompressed 1024-byte limit returning 413 for both codecs. No browser/proxy/HTTPS or third-party peer test.

humanProof.scope: Focused HTTP behavior runs locally without owner-only resources. Does not settle product-wide client/platform coverage or GA/publication gates.
